rows.stem:
(a) Write the molecular formula of the following carbon compounds :

(i) Methane

(ii) Propane

(b) Carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points. Why ?
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Methane: \(\mathrm{CH_4}\). (ii) Propane: \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\).

(b) Carbon compounds are made of molecules held together by covalent bonds, and the forces of attraction between these molecules are weak. Little energy is needed to overcome them, so the melting and boiling points are low.

rows.stem:
The electrons in the atoms of two elements X and Y are distributed in three shells having 1 and 7 electrons respectively in their outermost shells.

(a) Write the group numbers of these elements in the Modern Periodic Table.

(b) Write the molecular formula of the compound formed when X and Y combine with each other.

(c) Which of the two is electropositive ?
rows.solution:
Both elements have three shells. X has 1 electron in its outermost shell (2, 8, 1: sodium) and Y has 7 (2, 8, 7: chlorine).

(a) X is in group 1 and Y is in group 17.

(b) X loses one electron and Y gains one, so they combine in the ratio 1 : 1 and the formula is XY (as in NaCl).

(c) X is electropositive, since it loses its single valence electron easily to form a positive ion.

rows.stem:
(a) Which of the following flowers will have higher possibility of self-pollination ?

Mustard, Papaya, Watermelon, Hibiscus

(b) List the two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower.
rows.solution:
(a) Self-pollination is possible only in a bisexual flower, which has both stamens and pistil. Mustard and *Hibiscus* have bisexual flowers, so they have the higher possibility of self-pollination. Papaya and watermelon have unisexual flowers.

(b) Stamens (the male part) and pistil, or carpel (the female part).

rows.stem: Which one of the two multicellular organisms — Spirogyra and Planaria reproduces by regeneration and why ? Give an example of any other organism which can also reproduce by the same process.
rows.solution:
*Planaria* reproduces by regeneration. If its body is cut into pieces, each piece grows into a complete organism. Regeneration is carried out by specialised cells, which multiply and form the different cell types and tissues. *Spirogyra* does not have such specialised cells; its filament simply breaks into fragments that grow into new filaments (fragmentation).

*Hydra* also reproduces by regeneration.

rows.stem: What is variation ? List two main reasons that may lead to variation in a population.
rows.solution:
Variation is the difference in traits (characters) shown by the individuals of a species.

Two main reasons:

(i) Small inaccuracies (errors) in DNA copying during reproduction.

(ii) Sexual reproduction, which combines the DNA of two different parents.

rows.stem:
(i) In a cross between violet flowered plants and white flowered plants, state the characteristics of the plants obtained in the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny.

(ii) If the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny are self-pollinated, then what would be observed in the plants of \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny ?

(iii) If 100 plants are produced in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny, then how many plants will show the recessive trait ?
rows.solution:
(i) All the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are violet-flowered. No white-flowered plants appear, because violet is dominant over white.

(ii) The \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny has both violet-flowered and white-flowered plants, in the ratio of about 3 violet : 1 white.

(iii) The recessive trait (white flowers) appears in one-fourth of the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) plants, so \(\dfrac{1}{4} \times 100 = 25\) plants.

rows.stem:
(i) Name and state the rule to determine the direction of force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.

(ii) An alpha particle while passing through a magnetic field gets projected towards north. In which direction will an electron project when it passes through the same magnetic field ?
rows.solution:
(i) Fleming's left-hand rule. Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of motion of, or the force acting on, the conductor.

(ii) An electron carries a negative charge, opposite to the positive charge of an alpha particle. Moving the same way through the same field, it experiences a force in the opposite direction, so it is projected towards the south.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
(i) What is a solenoid ?

(ii) Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines of the magnetic field produced by a solenoid through which a steady current flows.
rows.solution:
(i) A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

(ii) Draw the solenoid connected to a battery and a key. Inside the solenoid the field lines are straight and parallel, showing a uniform field. Outside, the lines leave one end of the solenoid (which behaves as a north pole), curve round, and enter the other end (the south pole), so the pattern is like that of a bar magnet. Mark arrows on the lines: from south to north inside the solenoid and from north to south outside.

rows.stem: What is ozone ? How is it formed in the upper layers of the Earth’s atmosphere ? How does ozone affect our ecosystem ?
rows.solution:
Ozone is a molecule made of three atoms of oxygen, \(\mathrm{O_3}\).

In the upper atmosphere, ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun splits some oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms. These atoms combine with oxygen molecules to form ozone:

\(\mathrm{O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} O + O}\)

\(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\)

The ozone layer shields the surface of the earth from the harmful UV radiation of the sun, which can damage organisms (for example, by causing skin cancer). Depletion of the ozone layer therefore harms the organisms of the ecosystem.

rows.stem:
(i) List two human-made ecosystems.

(ii) “We do not clean a pond in the same manner as we do in an aquarium.” Give reason to justify this statement.
rows.solution:
(i) Any two: aquarium, crop field, garden, park.

(ii) A pond is a natural ecosystem. It has decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, which break down the dead remains and wastes and keep the pond clean. An aquarium is an artificial ecosystem without decomposers, so its wastes keep building up, and it needs regular cleaning to function properly.

rows.stem:
(a) List two advantages of adopting the atomic number of an element as the basis of classification of elements in the Modern Periodic Table.

(b) Write the electronic configurations of the elements X (atomic number 13) and Y (atomic number 20).
rows.solution:
(a) Any two:

(i) The atomic number is a more fundamental property of an element than its atomic mass, and it decides the properties of the element.

(ii) The atomic number increases by one in going from one element to the next, so the arrangement of elements becomes more systematic.

(iii) Properties of elements can be predicted with more precision when the elements are arranged in increasing order of their atomic numbers.

(b) X (atomic number 13): 2, 8, 3.

Y (atomic number 20): 2, 8, 8, 2.

rows.stem: Draw two different possible structures of a saturated hydrocarbon having four carbon atoms in its molecule. What are these two structures of the hydrocarbon having same molecular formula called ? Write the molecular formula and the common name of this compound. Also write the molecular formula of its alkyne.
rows.solution:
A saturated hydrocarbon with four carbon atoms is butane, \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\). Its four carbon atoms can be arranged in two ways:

1. A straight chain: four carbon atoms joined in a row by single bonds, each end carbon carrying three hydrogens and each middle carbon two hydrogens (\(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\)).

2. A branched chain: a chain of three carbon atoms with the fourth carbon (as a \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) group) attached to the middle carbon. The middle carbon carries one hydrogen and each of the three end carbons carries three hydrogens (\(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_3}\)).

Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called structural isomers.

The molecular formula is \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\) and the common name is butane.

The alkyne with four carbon atoms (butyne) has the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_4H_6}\).

rows.stem:
(i) Write the molecular formula of benzene and draw its structure.

(ii) Write the number of single and double covalent bonds present in a molecule of benzene.

(iii) Which compounds are called alkynes ?
rows.solution:
(i) The molecular formula of benzene is \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\).

Structure: six carbon atoms form a hexagonal ring, joined by alternate single and double bonds (three of each), and each carbon atom carries one hydrogen atom.

(ii) Single covalent bonds: 9 (6 carbon-hydrogen bonds and 3 carbon-carbon single bonds). Double covalent bonds: 3 (all carbon-carbon).

(iii) Hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon triple bond are called alkynes (general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}\)).

rows.stem:
(a) Mention one function each of the following organs in human male reproductive system :

(i) Testis

(ii) Scrotum

(iii) Vas deferens

(iv) Prostate gland

(b) Name the type of germ cell which (i) is motile, and (ii) stores food.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Testis: produces the male gametes (sperms); it also secretes the male sex hormone, testosterone.

(ii) Scrotum: holds the testes outside the abdominal cavity, at a temperature lower than the body temperature, which sperm formation needs.

(iii) Vas deferens: transports the sperms from the testis towards the urethra.

(iv) Prostate gland: secretes a fluid that makes the transport of sperms easier and provides them nutrition.

(b) (i) The sperm (male germ cell) is motile. (ii) The egg, or ovum (female germ cell), stores food.

rows.stem:
(a) Three resistors \(\mathrm{R_1}\), \(\mathrm{R_2}\) and \(\mathrm{R_3}\) are connected in parallel and the combination is connected to a battery, an ammeter, a voltmeter and a key. Draw suitable circuit diagram to show the arrangement of these circuit components along with the direction of current flowing.

(b) Calculate the equivalent resistance of the following network :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (b) gives its network only as a drawing: terminals A and B, junctions C and D, and four resistors labelled \(\mathrm{R_1} = 5\,\Omega\), \(\mathrm{R_2} = 10\,\Omega\), \(\mathrm{R_3} = 10\,\Omega\) and \(\mathrm{R_4} = 5\,\Omega\); how they are connected between A and B is left to the drawing, since it decides the answer. Part (a) is a diagram the student draws. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
(a) Circuit diagram: join \(\mathrm{R_1}\), \(\mathrm{R_2}\) and \(\mathrm{R_3}\) side by side between two common junctions, so they are in parallel. Connect this combination in series with the battery, the key and the ammeter. Connect the voltmeter across the two junctions, in parallel with the combination. The positive terminals of the ammeter and the voltmeter go towards the positive terminal of the battery.

Mark the current with arrows: it flows out of the positive terminal of the battery, divides at the first junction into the three resistors, recombines at the second junction, and returns through the key and the ammeter to the negative terminal.

(b) \(\mathrm{R_2}\) and \(\mathrm{R_3}\) are in parallel between C and D:

\(\dfrac{1}{R_{CD}} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{2}{10} = \dfrac{1}{5}\), so \(R_{CD} = 5\,\Omega\).

\(\mathrm{R_1}\) (between A and C), \(R_{CD}\) and \(\mathrm{R_4}\) (between D and B) are in series:

\(R_{AB} = R_1 + R_{CD} + R_4 = 5\,\Omega + 5\,\Omega + 5\,\Omega = 15\,\Omega\).

rows.stem:
(i) Define Electric Power and write its SI unit.

(ii) Two bulbs rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to an electric mains of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the bulbs from the mains.
rows.solution:
(i) Electric power is the rate at which electric energy is dissipated or consumed in an electric circuit. Its SI unit is the watt (W), which is 1 joule per second (or 1 volt ampere).

(ii) Each bulb gets the full 220 V, since they are in parallel. Using \(P = VI\):

\(I_1 = \dfrac{100}{220}\) A and \(I_2 = \dfrac{60}{220}\) A.

Total current drawn from the mains:

\(I = I_1 + I_2 = \dfrac{100 + 60}{220} = \dfrac{160}{220} \approx 0{\cdot}73\) A.

rows.stem:
(i) State Joule’s law of heating. Express it mathematically when an appliance of resistance R is connected to a source of voltage V and the current I flows through the appliance for a time t.

(ii) A \(5\,\Omega\) resistor is connected across a battery of 6 volts. Calculate the energy that dissipates as heat in 10 s.
rows.solution:
(i) Joule's law of heating: the heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current for a given resistance, directly proportional to the resistance for a given current, and directly proportional to the time for which the current flows.

Mathematically, \(H = I^2Rt\). Since \(V = IR\), this is also \(H = VIt = \dfrac{V^2}{R}t\).

(ii) \(V = 6\) V, \(R = 5\,\Omega\), \(t = 10\) s.

\(H = \dfrac{V^2}{R}t = \dfrac{(6)^2}{5} \times 10 = \dfrac{36}{5} \times 10 = 72\) J.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the group of organisms which form in the first trophic level of all food chains. Why are they called so ?

(b) Why are the human beings most adversely affected by bio-magnification ?

(c) State one ill-effect of the absence of decomposers from a natural ecosystem.
rows.solution:
(a) Producers (green plants). They make their own food from simple inorganic substances by photosynthesis, using sunlight, and so start every food chain.

(b) Non-biodegradable harmful chemicals, such as pesticides like DDT, enter a food chain and accumulate progressively at each trophic level. Human beings occupy the top level in most food chains, so the maximum concentration of these chemicals accumulates in their bodies.

(c) Any one: dead bodies and wastes would pile up on the earth, with a foul smell; minerals would not be recycled; the soil would not be replenished with nutrients; the ecosystem would be disrupted.

rows.stem: Why is a pair of sex chromosomes in human beings called a mismatched pair in terms of type and size ?
rows.context: The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not. There are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes in human beings. Out of these, 44 (22 pairs) control the body characters and 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.
rows.solution: In a human male the sex chromosomes are X and Y. They are of different types, and the Y chromosome is much shorter than the X chromosome, so the pair is mismatched.

rows.stem: Out of male or female, which of them has a perfect pair of sex chromosomes ? In case of a perfect pair, will the gametes produced be of the same kind or of a different kind ?
rows.context: The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not. There are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes in human beings. Out of these, 44 (22 pairs) control the body characters and 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.
rows.solution: The female (mother) has a perfect pair, XX. All the gametes (eggs) she produces are of the same kind: each carries an X chromosome.

rows.stem: Name two animals whose sex is not genetically determined. Explain the process of their sex determination.
rows.context: The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not. There are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes in human beings. Out of these, 44 (22 pairs) control the body characters and 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.
rows.solution:
Some reptiles and snails.

In some reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept decides whether the animal developing in the egg will be a male or a female.

In snails, an individual can change its sex during its lifetime, so sex is not genetically fixed.

rows.stem: With the help of a flowchart only, show how sex is genetically determined in human beings.
rows.context: The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not. There are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes in human beings. Out of these, 44 (22 pairs) control the body characters and 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.
rows.solution:
Flowchart (label each step):

Male (44 + XY) \(\rightarrow\) sperms of two kinds: X-carrying and Y-carrying.

Female (44 + XX) \(\rightarrow\) eggs of one kind only: X-carrying.

Sperm with X + egg with X \(\rightarrow\) zygote XX \(\rightarrow\) female child (girl).

Sperm with Y + egg with X \(\rightarrow\) zygote XY \(\rightarrow\) male child (boy).

So the sex of the child depends on whether the sperm that fertilises the egg carries an X or a Y chromosome.

rows.stem: Draw a diagram to show this pattern of iron filings.
rows.context: A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board using some adhesive materials. She places a bar magnet in the centre of it and sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet using a salt-sprinkler. On tapping the board gently, she observes that the iron filings have arranged themselves in a particular pattern.
rows.solution: Draw the bar magnet in the centre with its ends marked N and S. The iron filings gather most densely at the two ends (the poles) and arrange themselves in curved lines that run from one end of the magnet round to the other, crowded near the poles and spreading out farther away.

rows.stem: Draw the magnetic field lines of a bar magnet showing the poles of the bar magnet as well as the direction of the magnetic field lines.
rows.context: A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board using some adhesive materials. She places a bar magnet in the centre of it and sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet using a salt-sprinkler. On tapping the board gently, she observes that the iron filings have arranged themselves in a particular pattern.
rows.solution: Draw the bar magnet with its north (N) and south (S) poles marked. Draw closed curves that emerge from the north pole, curve round outside the magnet and enter the south pole; inside the magnet they continue from the south pole to the north pole. Put arrows on the lines in this direction. The lines are crowded near the poles, where the field is strongest, and none of them cross.

rows.stem: How is the direction of magnetic field at a point determined using the field lines ? Why do two magnetic field lines not cross each other ?
rows.context: A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board using some adhesive materials. She places a bar magnet in the centre of it and sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet using a salt-sprinkler. On tapping the board gently, she observes that the iron filings have arranged themselves in a particular pattern.
rows.solution:
Place a compass needle on a field line: the direction in which its north pole points gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point. (The tangent to the field line at the point gives the same direction.)

Two field lines never cross, because at the point of intersection the compass needle would have to point in two directions at once, meaning the field would have two directions at one point. This is not possible.

rows.stem: How are the magnetic field lines of a bar magnet drawn using a small compass needle ? Draw one magnetic field line each on both sides of the magnet.
rows.context: A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board using some adhesive materials. She places a bar magnet in the centre of it and sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet using a salt-sprinkler. On tapping the board gently, she observes that the iron filings have arranged themselves in a particular pattern.
rows.solution:
Place a small bar magnet at the centre of a sheet of white paper fixed on a drawing board and mark its boundary.

Place a small compass near the north pole of the magnet. Its south pole points towards the north pole of the magnet and its north pole away from it. Mark the positions of the two ends of the needle.

Move the compass so that its south end occupies the position just marked for its north end, and mark the new position of the north end. Proceed step by step in this way until you reach the south pole of the magnet. Join the marked points with a smooth curve: this is one field line. Repeat the process on the other side of the magnet to get a second field line.

Diagram: the magnet with N and S marked, one curved line above it and one below, each running from the north pole round to the south pole, with arrows pointing from N to S along the curves.
